name: _newselect
synopsis: int select(int nfds, fd_set *_Nullable restrict readfds, fd_set *_Nullable restrict writefds, fd_set *_Nullable restrict exceptfds, struct timeval *_Nullable restrict timeout);

int pselect(int nfds, fd_set *_Nullable restrict readfds, fd_set *_Nullable restrict writefds, fd_set *_Nullable restrict exceptfds, const struct timespec *_Nullable restrict timeout, const sigset_t *_Nullable restrict sigmask);
description: select() allows a program to monitor multiple file descriptors, waiting until one or more become ready for I/O operations such as reading or writing. It uses sets to specify descriptors for readability, writability, or exceptions, but is limited by FD_SETSIZE and is recommended to be replaced by poll or epoll for modern applications.

parameters.name: nfds
parameters.description: The highest file descriptor to check plus one.

parameters.name: readfds
parameters.description: Set of file descriptors to monitor for readability.

parameters.name: writefds
parameters.description: Set of file descriptors to monitor for writability.

parameters.name: exceptfds
parameters.description: Set of file descriptors to monitor for exceptions.

return_value.success: Returns the number of ready file descriptors
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: An invalid file descriptor was given in one of the sets.
nfds is negative or exceeds limits, or timeout is invalid.
Unable to allocate memory for internal tables.

bugs: select() is limited by FD_SETSIZE (1024), modifies fd_set in place, may ignore invalid file descriptors greater than the process's maximum, and has had race conditions in pselect emulation; it may also report spurious readiness on sockets.
